reasons.A: Long, winding, qualified sentences with semicolons and asides, and a dry, courteous irony towards the great man; this is closest to the passage's periodic movement and mock-formal stance, though its polish runs slightly smoother than the original.
reasons.B: Has the right deadpan irony and the comic catalogue, but its clipped, staccato short sentences ('It was drawn out.') are a modern mannerism that the passage's long, clause-heavy rhythm lacks.
reasons.C: Plain, explanatory and sympathetic, and it disclaims mockery outright; it summarises instead of playing out the scene with wry commentary, so it has neither the passage's ironic stance nor its convoluted syntax.
